name: libpst
desc: Utilities for the PST file format
why: Utilities for decoding Outlook PST files let you dig into a proprietary, obscure file format.

brief.what_it_is: libpst is a set of command-line utilities for reading Microsoft Outlook Personal Folders (.pst) files. It takes a PST file as input and produces mbox or MH mailbox folders (readpst), a listing of the file's contents (lspst), contacts as LDIF for LDAP import (pst2ldif), and email messages as DII load files for CT Summation products (pst2dii). The homepage also mentions contacts converting to a simple list or vCard. The homepage lists nick2ldif as an installed executable but does not describe it. The homepage advertises version 0.6.76.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the project exists to convert Outlook PST files, which the page describes as covering both 32-bit files from before Outlook 2003 and 64-bit Outlook 2003 files, into formats other tools can read. The README's framing is 'Utilities for the PST file format'. The homepage points to libpff for documentation of the format.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. It names a shared library with developer documentation at /libpst/devel/, so the utilities are built on that library. The page does not describe the parsing approach.
brief.install_notes: The homepage points to source and binary packages at http://www.five-ten-sg.com/libpst/packages/ and a Mercurial source repository at http://hg.five-ten-sg.com/libpst/. The brew formula's executables are lspst, nick2ldif, pst2ldif and readpst. No commands or setup steps appeared on the homepage, and I could not load the readpst documentation page.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, narrow tool for a proprietary, obscure file format, and it covers both old 32-bit and Outlook 2003 64-bit PST files. It also writes DII load files, which suggests a legal-discovery or e-discovery audience.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows: it advertises version 0.6.76 and links to packages and a Mercurial repository. The page shows no release or commit dates, so I could not confirm how recent the release is.
brief.caveats: The homepage only states support for 32-bit files from before Outlook 2003 and 64-bit Outlook 2003 files. It says nothing about newer Outlook PST versions, so check that before relying on it. The documentation page for readpst returned 404 under the two URLs I guessed. No license or platform information appeared on the homepage. The homepage was reachable, so these gaps come from the page content, not from a failed fetch.
quotes: This version can now convert both 32 bit Outlook files (pre 2003), and the 64 bit Outlook 2003 pst files.
Utilities are supplied to convert email messages to both mbox and MH mailbox formats, and to DII load file format for use with many of the CT Summation products.
Contacts can be converted to a simple list, to vcard format, or to ldif format for import to an LDAP server.
